name: fetch_datasets_from_google_sheet
title: Google Sheets Dataset Fetcher
author: Generated by Botcraft
short_description: Fetches datasets from Google Sheets using API credentials and specified range
long_description: This machine connects to Google Sheets API v4 to fetch data from a specified spreadsheet and range. It authenticates using the provided API key, retrieves the data from the exact sheet ID and range specified, and returns a structured dataset with headers and rows. The machine supports A1 notation for ranges and handles empty cells gracefully.

specification.input:
• google_sheet_id: String - The unique identifier of the Google Sheet to fetch data from
  • google_api_key: String - Google API key for authentication with Google Sheets API
  • google_sheet_range: String - The range in A1 notation (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:D10') to fetch from the sheet
specification.output:
• status: String - Operation status (success or error)
  • action: String - The action performed (fetch_google_sheet_data)
  • result: Object - Contains the fetched dataset with headers and rows
  • error: String - Error message if operation failed, empty on success
  • metadata: Object - Contains sheet_name, total_rows, and total_columns

parameters.detail: The unique identifier of the Google Sheet. Found in the sheet URL between /d/ and /edit
Google API key with Google Sheets API access enabled. Keep this credential secure
The range to fetch in A1 notation (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:D10' or 'A:A' for entire column)

faq.question: What format should the Google Sheet range be in?
faq.answer: Use A1 notation like 'Sheet1!A1:D10' for a specific range, 'A:A' for an entire column, '1:1' for an entire row, or 'Sheet1' for the entire sheet.

faq.question: How do I find my Google Sheet ID?
faq.answer: The Sheet ID is the long string in your Google Sheets URL between '/d/' and '/edit'. For example, in 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ABC123DEF456/edit', the ID is '1ABC123DEF456'.

faq.question: What happens if the specified range is empty?
faq.answer: The machine will return an empty dataset with no rows rather than an error. This allows graceful handling of empty ranges.

faq.question: Do I need special permissions for the Google API key?
faq.answer: Yes, your API key must have the Google Sheets API enabled in the Google Cloud Console, and the sheet must be either public or shared with the service account associated with the API key.
